subject: Latency & throughput tradeoffs — hosted vs dedicated (post-demo clarifications)
messages:
From: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Ellis <j.ellis@speedcommerce.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 10 Apr 2028 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Latency & throughput tradeoffs — hosted vs dedicated (post-demo clarifications)

Jordan — thanks again for taking the demo today. Quick recap + a couple of follow-ups so we can narrow the deployment recommendation for SpeedCommerce's search pipeline.

Key signals from the call:
- Traffic profile: avg 2.5k QPS during peak events (promotions) with spiky bursts to ~6k QPS for short windows (~5–10m).
- Latency target: p95 end-to-end inference <= 120ms for single-turn product search responses.
- Payload: typical prompt length ~120 tokens; responses ~60 tokens.
- Data concerns: PCI-adjacent logs; would prefer not to route search queries through a multi-tenant stack if avoidable.

Open clarifying asks (two quick ones):
1) Can you confirm whether the 6k QPS bursts are global or concentrated in a single region? (You mentioned US East primarily.)
2) Are there hard restrictions on cache duration for product embeddings (TTL) vs freshness requirements?

Based on what we heard, two high-level options look relevant: Hosted API (fast to onboard, lower ops) vs Dedicated (reserved GPU pools for predictable throughput and isolated compute). We'll sketch a recommended pilot in the follow-up mail once we get the two datapoints above.

Attachment: pilot_sla_draft.pdf (draft SLOs/pilot scope)

Thanks — Rafael
Rafael Mendes
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
rafel.mendes@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0193

From: Jordan Ellis <j.ellis@speedcommerce.com>

Cc: ops@speedcommerce.com
Date: Tue, 10 Apr 2028 16:07:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Latency & throughput tradeoffs — hosted vs dedicated (post-demo clarifications)

Rafael — thanks for the clear recap. Two quick answers:

- Bursts are primarily US-East (NY/NJ) — global traffic is minimal today. We do have occasional flash traffic from CA and EU but <=10% of the bursts.
- Embedding freshness: product catalog updates every 15 minutes; for search relevance we need new vectors reflected within 30 minutes of a catalog update. TTL can be short but freshness is important.

Also uploaded a quick CSV with observed qps/latency samples from last month's promo to the ops alias — see qps_latency_samples.csv.

If helpful, we can do a 30m technical sync with your infra engineer to walk live through spike patterns.

— Jordan
Jordan Ellis
Head of Search Engineering, SpeedCommerce
j.ellis@speedcommerce.com
From: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Jordan Ellis <j.ellis@speedcommerce.com>
Date: Wed, 11 Apr 2028 08:14:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Latency & throughput tradeoffs — hosted vs dedicated (post-demo clarifications)

Marissa/Ben — forwarding Jordan's answers and the CSV. Quick internal read: given US-east concentration + need for sub-30m embedding freshness + p95 <=120ms, I think we should recommend a two-stage pilot:

Stage A (Pilot, 4 weeks) — Hosted API, performance-guarded:
- Start on Hosted with warmed prefix cache and adaptive batching; run in US-east region.
- Capacity reservation: short burst buffer (burst credits) enabled to handle the first 6k spikes while we collect telemetry.
- Goals: validate latency SLO on production traffic and ensure embedding refresh sync works with TTLs.
- Risk: multi-tenant variability; might not hit strict p95 with heavier model choices.

Stage B (if Stage A fails p95) — Fast follow to Dedicated (2–4 week cutover):
- Reserved GPU pool (N nodes) pinned to the pilot model variant; autoscale rules tuned for burst windows.
- Migration plan: model pinning + routing policy for fallback to hosted if dedicated reaches capacity.
- Goals: stable p95, predictable unit economics during promo traffic.

Ask: can we propose the above two-stage plan to Jordan and offer a 30m infra sync this week? Also I attached a draft SLA scope (pilot_sla_draft.pdf) to share.

Thoughts on sizing: based on CSV sample (Jordan) and our perf profiles, initial Dedicated sizing likely 6 x A100-equivalent nodes for headroom; we can tune after 1–2 days of warm traffic.

Rafael
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 11 Apr 2028 10:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Latency & throughput tradeoffs — hosted vs dedicated (post-demo clarifications)

Thanks — good decomposition. A couple quick internal nitpoints before we present:
- Recommendation: lead with Hosted pilot only if Jordan agrees to an aggressive cache-warm plan + SLA windows (we should get explicit p95 acceptance criteria in writing).
- Confirm that embedding sync can be pushed via our ingestion hook (we have a 1–2 minute propagation path to our vector store on Hosted). If SpeedCommerce wants stricter guarantees, Dedicated is the right path.
- Pricing note: include a reserved capacity quote for the Dedicated fallback in the proposal (monthly commit + hourly burst pricing). I'll draft numbers and Ben can sanity-check.

Ben — can you draft the initial dedicated sizing estimate (cost/week and expected p95 improvement) and put it in the HubSpot deal notes? I linked the runbook that explains the dedicated cutover path: https://redwood.example.com/runbooks/deploy-mode-cheatsheet

I'll prepare a short customer-facing note that proposes the two-stage pilot (Hosted -> Dedicated fallback) and proposes 30m sync options (Thu 1300–1500 PT or Fri 0900–1100 PT). Rafael — happy for you to send that to Jordan.

— Marissa
VP, Solutions & GTM Operations, Redwood Inference
